subtitle: Retrieval that works on product data: chunking, embeddings, hybrid search, reranking, and grounded answers — build the RAG layer behind a store's assistant
audience: Developers who finished Prompt Engineering 101 and OpenDataLoader PDF (chunking, validation, TF-IDF baselines) and now connect retrieval to generation on catalog, policy, and order data. Retrieval machinery runs as executable JS in the playground; embedding/vector-store calls target your own project with provider-neutral patterns.
outcomes: Explain why RAG exists (freshness, grounding, cost) and map the full pipeline stage by stage
Chunk product catalogs into retrievable units with SKU/category/price/version metadata
Use embeddings and cosine similarity correctly — and know what they capture and miss
Fuse keyword and vector retrieval with hybrid strategies and RRF-style score fusion
Rewrite vague shopper queries (multi-query, step-back, filter extraction) before retrieval
Rerank candidates with score fusion and top-k discipline under cost constraints
Generate grounded answers with citations, abstention paths, and staleness guards
Evaluate RAG with hit-rate, faithfulness checks, and failure-taxonomy gold sets
Route agentic RAG (answer-direct vs retrieve vs tools vs escalate) with loop budgets
Ship a store-assistant RAG layer with measured retrieval and grounded generation

assessment.q: Catalog prices change hourly. Fine-tune vs RAG?
options: RAG: retrieval reads current prices at query time — freshness without retraining; fine-tuning bakes static knowledge
assessment.explain: Freshness is RAG's core reason: dynamic data stays in the store, retrieved live. Fine-tuning freezes knowledge at train time (Ch.1).

options: One chunk per catalog, variants omitted
Per-variant retrievable units with SKU/price/version metadata — variants differ on exactly what shoppers ask
assessment.explain: Chunk boundaries follow question boundaries: shoppers ask variant-level questions, so units carry variant-level metadata (Ch.2).

assessment.q: Embeddings retrieve 'reimbursement' for query 'refund'. TF-IDF returns nothing. Meaning?
options: Semantic vs lexical gap: embeddings capture meaning overlap, TF-IDF needs term overlap — the hybrid case for fusing both
assessment.explain: Complementary miss profiles motivate hybrid retrieval: each covers the other's blind spot (Ch.3–4).

assessment.q: 'Something for my feet, cheap' as a shopper query. First move?
options: Rewrite: expand to concrete candidates (shoes/sneakers/sandals) + extract budget filter — vague queries need interpretation before retrieval
assessment.explain: Vague queries fail retrieval literally. Multi-query expansion + filter extraction translate intent into retrievable form (Ch.5).

assessment.q: Reranker budget allows 50 candidates but retrieval returns 500. Setup?
options: Funnel: cheap first-stage retrieval (TF-IDF/vector top-200) → rerank top-50 → generate from top-5 — cost-tiered pipeline
assessment.explain: Rerankers are precise and pricey: funnels match cost tiers to stages (cheap recall, precise rerank, minimal generation context) (Ch.6).

assessment.q: Answer cites a price with no source span. Handling?
options: Quarantine: uncited specifics fail grounding checks; regenerate with citation demands or abstain — staleness quarantines, not ships
assessment.explain: Grounded generation requires source spans per claim, especially money. Uncited specifics are hallucination signatures (Ch.7).

assessment.q: RAG retrieves the right doc but answers unsupportedly. Investigate first?
options: Generation: context present but unused/overridden — check scope-to-context rules, citation demands, and context position effects
assessment.explain: Right-doc-wrong-answer localizes to generation: grounding rules, citation enforcement, and attention position — not retrieval (Ch.8).

assessment.q: 'Do you price-match?' (policy) vs 'Where is order 4821?' (lookup). Router?
options: Policy → RAG retrieval; lookup → order tool; greetings → direct answer — route by information need, with confidence fallback to retrieval
assessment.explain: Agentic RAG routes by need: static knowledge→retrieve, live records→tools, chitchat→direct, uncertainty→safe default. One path per need (Ch.9).

assessment.q: Multi-hop retrieval loops 'specs → compatible accessories → price'. Guard?
options: Hop budget + done-condition (answer complete?) + visited-set against cycles — retrieval loops terminate by construction
assessment.explain: Iterative retrieval is managed looping: budgets, completion criteria, cycle guards — same termination discipline as agent loops (Ch.9).

assessment.q: Hit-rate 9/10 but the miss is a $500 price answer. Verdict?
options: Segment by stakes: money answers need 100% grounding enforcement (citations + staleness checks), not average hit-rates — severity-weighted eval
assessment.explain: Averages hide severity: price errors cost real money. Eval weights by stakes with hard gates on money claims (Ch.8 + capstone).

assessment.q: Chunk without SKU metadata answers correctly. Problem?
options: Uncitable and unfilterable: correctness without provenance can't be verified, filtered, or freshness-checked — metadata is load-bearing
assessment.explain: Metadata enables citations, filtering, and staleness checks. Correct-but-orphaned answers fail production requirements silently (Ch.2).

assessment.q: v2 chunking beats v1 hit-rate but breaks price citations. Ship?
options: No: per-metric no-regression gate — retrieval gains must not cost grounding; fix citations first (same eval discipline, RAG flavor)
assessment.explain: Multi-metric gates: hit-rate AND faithfulness must hold. Trading grounding for retrieval is a regression wearing an improvement costume (Ch.8).

project.title: The Store-Assistant RAG Layer
project.summary: Build the RAG layer behind a shoe-store assistant: chunked catalog + policy corpus with metadata, hybrid retrieval with reranking, grounded generation with citations, agentic routing (retrieve/tools/direct/escalate), and a gold-set evaluation with per-segment truth. Measured retrieval, honest grounding.
requirements: Corpus: 20+ product/policy chunks with SKU/category/price/version metadata and as-of dates
Retrieval: TF-IDF baseline + hybrid fusion + reranked top-k with staged funnel (cheap recall → precise rerank → minimal context)
Query layer: rewriter (expansion + filter extraction) with before/after retrieval comparisons on 5 vague queries
Generation: scope-to-context contracts, citation demands, abstention path, staleness guard on prices
Agentic router: retrieve/tools/direct/escalate with routing tests and loop budgets
Evaluation: 15-question gold set (in-stock/policy/price/edge/attack) with hit-rate + faithfulness scores and failure taxonomy
technical: Retrieval machinery in runnable JS (playground-verified); embedding/vector calls in your project with provider-neutral patterns
Every chunk carries provenance metadata; every money claim carries citations + freshness
Router tests enumerated; loop budgets enforced; quarantine paths demonstrated
Numbers reproducible: gold set + chunker parameters committed
project.architecture: Four sections: (1) Corpus & chunking — units, metadata schema, version policy; (2) Retrieval — stages, fusion, rerank, router with budgets; (3) Generation — contracts, citations, abstention, staleness guards; (4) Evaluation — gold scores per segment, failure taxonomy, iterated fix with delta.
steps: Build the corpus: chunk catalog + policies with full metadata and dates
Implement retrieval stages with TF-IDF baseline first; add hybrid + rerank with measured deltas
Add rewriting; prove gains on 5 vague queries before/after
Write generation contracts with citations + abstention; enforce staleness on prices
Add the agentic router with tests and budgets; run the gold set; iterate once; re-score
Write the findings with per-segment truth and the deferred list
evaluation: Metadata complete on all chunks (SKU/category/price/version/date where applicable)
Retrieval staged with measured stage contributions; rerank justified by delta
Rewriting proven on vague queries with before/after comparisons
Money claims cited + fresh or abstained; no silent staleness
Gold baseline + iteration with per-segment diffs; failures taxonomized
stretch: Add multi-hop retrieval for 'compatible accessories' questions with cycle guards
Benchmark chunk sizes (200 vs 500 vs 1000 chars) on hit-rate with cost noted
Convert one retrieval path to embeddings and report the lexical-vs-semantic miss swap

interviewQs.q: RAG vs fine-tuning — decide for hourly-changing prices.
interviewQs.a: RAG: prices live in the store, retrieved fresh per query — no retraining, always current. Fine-tuning bakes knowledge at train time: stale within the hour, expensive to refresh, and incapable of citing sources. Rule: dynamic/factual/citable → RAG; stable style/reasoning patterns → fine-tuning. Most production systems combine both (tuned behavior over retrieved facts).

interviewQs.q: Right document retrieved, unsupported answer. Debug order?
interviewQs.a: Generation side first: scope-to-context rules present? citation demands enforced? decisive evidence positioned for recency? Then context assembly (truncation cut the span? ordering buried it?), then retrieval scoring (was it top-1 or rank-9 filler?). Right-doc-wrong-answer exonerates retrieval — investigate the consumer, not the retriever.

interviewQs.q: Hybrid retrieval: why fuse, and how?
interviewQs.a: Lexical (TF-IDF/BM25) wins exact terms, SKUs, names; vector wins paraphrase and semantics. Fuse with staged pipelines (cheap recall from both, union) plus reranking, or score fusion (RRF/normalized weighted sums) — measured per corpus. Fuse because miss profiles complement: each covers the other's blindness (vocabulary mismatch vs term tyranny).

interviewQs.q: How do you keep RAG prices from lying?
interviewQs.a: As-of dates on chunks, freshness recency in ranking, staleness guards (reject/flag aged prices), citations binding claims to spans, and abstention when sources lack current data. Price claims get hard gates, not average hit-rates: severity-weighted eval with 100% grounding enforcement on money.

interviewQs.q: When does RAG need an agent around it?
interviewQs.a: When needs vary per query (lookup vs policy vs chitchat → router), retrieval must iterate (multi-hop with budgets), or tools join sources (orders DB + catalog). Static single-shot Q&A stays a pipeline; variable, multi-source, multi-step needs agentic routing with loop budgets and escalation paths.

interviewQs.q: Chunking strategy for a product catalog — defend it.
interviewQs.a: Per-variant units (shoppers ask variant questions) with SKU/price/version/date metadata; overlap for boundary recall; section-aware cuts (specs vs reviews separate); as-of dating for freshness. Boundaries follow question boundaries; metadata enables citations, filtering, and staleness checks. Measured by hit-rate deltas on vague + precise gold queries, not by aesthetics.
